patch.value: Bound manifest metadata so a fragmented file's memory ceiling does not scale with its length

A fragment manifest holds one entry per fragment, so its size grows with totalLength divided by fragmentSize. writeFragmentedFile retains every entry and returns the whole manifest, encodeManifest builds all lines into one buffer, and decodeManifest splits the full payload and retains every entry. The content path is genuinely streaming after the corrected proofs, but the metadata path is not, so the fixed memory ceiling the feature promises does not hold at the top of the size range. At the 1 MiB default fragment size a 1 GiB file is about 1024 entries, which is unremarkable, and a 1 TiB file is about a million entries, which is not. The likely shape is a multi-level manifest so a reader touches only the entries covering the range it asked for, which is also what makes a range read on a very large file cheap.

Peak metadata memory for a read and for a range read is bounded independently of totalLength, proven the same way the content proofs are: sample while the operation is in flight and fail against an implementation that materializes every entry; encode and decode do not require the whole manifest resident; existing manifests remain readable

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Audit 2026-09-13: EXISTS — content streaming is implemented (engine/fragments.ts: writeFragmentedFile reads the source in bounded chunks, peak heap bounded by fragmentSize). Range reads touch only overlapping fragments (test/fragments.test.ts). REMAINS — the manifest metadata path is NOT bounded independently of totalLength: writeFragmentedFile materializes the full manifest entry list (line 158: peak heap bounded by fragmentSize plus the manifest entry list), encodeManifest builds all lines into one buffer, and decodeManifest splits the full payload. No multi-level manifest exists (grep for multi-level/level manifest returns no matches). A 1 TiB file at 1 MiB fragments would produce about a million manifest entries, all resident. The acceptance criteria require peak metadata memory bounded independently of totalLength and encode/decode not requiring the whole manifest resident.

value.text: Independent design review: the bounded format must prove streaming writer and read/range behavior while operations are in flight, with unchanged production functions reverted. Check retained legacy v1 reads explicitly: decoding a large v1 object into its full entry array remains a metadata growth path, so either bound that reader too or make the legacy compatibility boundary explicit and verify it against the written acceptance criteria. Also exercise height/count/length validation and closure, bundle and erasure behavior for interior nodes.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Independent review requested a stronger measurement before full gates: counting entries in each individual physical node cannot detect a reader retaining all nodes or flattening all entries. Read and range regressions must also fail for behaviorally correct full-list materialization, and large legacy v1 read behavior must satisfy the stated metadata bound.

Legacy compatibility now uses a backpressured decompression worker and bounded canonical line traversal while preserving synchronous callers. Behavioral full-list reverts will be measured separately.
